reasoning.text: Biggest reproducibility gap: the spec pins the functional parameters (N=1024, 8 BUs, 14-bit, Barrett) but omits the exact modulus q, twiddle/root values, Barrett constants, the conflict-free address-generation equations, and the FSM schedule — so both teams had to guess q and the transform flavor and could only rebuild a behaviorally-correct round-trip, not the same hardware. Biggest fidelity gap: the reference's two signature contributions — the conflict-free memory mapping and the quantified 33%/20% radix-4 reductions — are not actually realized (one impl even shows the textbook butterfly yields 25%/0%), and both chose cyclic over the PQC-typical negacyclic transform, making these generic correct NTT cores rather than the specific CFNTT architecture.
gaps: [param] Exact modulus q (only '14-bit NTT-friendly prime' given; no concrete value)
[operation] Transform flavor: cyclic vs negacyclic (and psi 2N-th-root twist location)
[param] Primitive root / twiddle-factor values, ROM depth, contents and addressing
[param] Barrett parameters: bit-width k, precomputed mu, shift amount, number of conditional corrections
[control] Conflict-free address-generation equations (bank-index and offset functions) — the paper's headline contribution, only asserted as a property
[control] Schedule/FSM state set and the 'rearranged loop order' that yields the 33% mult / 20% add-sub savings
[control] Radix-2/4 selector semantics and how 8 lanes map onto 4-input radix-4 butterflies
[timing] Pipeline depth / latency of multiplier, adder/subtractor, reduction stage and the array
[port] FIFO depths, port widths, and handshake (valid/ready) protocol
[port] Crossbar / operand-read / operand-return bus signal widths and directions
[width] Datapath widths beyond the 14-bit coefficient (28-bit product, ~42-bit Barrett intermediate)

+ def ntt_radix4(x, w):
+     """Recursive radix-4 NTT (n must be a power of 4): splits into 4 phases,
+     independent of the radix-2 routine -> cross-check of the scalable datapath."""
+     n = len(x)
+     if n == 1:
+         return [x[0] % Q]
+     sub = [ntt_radix4(x[r::4], pow(w, 4, Q)) for r in range(4)]
+     wpow = [pow(w, i, Q) for i in range(n)]
+     m = n // 4
+     X = [0] * n
+     for k in range(n):
+         kk = k % m
+         acc = 0
+         for r in range(4):
+             acc = modadd(acc, modmul(wpow[(r * k) % n], sub[r][kk]))
+         X[k] = acc
+     return X
